# Large multi-feature tasks

When a request is big — multiple features, or a large ask that naturally splits into independent
pieces of work — do not implement it as one monolithic pass. Split it into separate commits, one
per feature/unit of work, and drive each unit through this graph-engineering framework using the
Agent tool:

```
Task -> Planner -> Worker -> [Reviewer 1, Reviewer 2, ... Reviewer N] -> Synthesise -> Pass?
                     ^                                                        |
                     |-------------------- feedback (no) ---------------------|
                                                                               |
                                                                          (yes) -> commit -> next unit
```

- **Planner**: breaks the overall ask into an ordered list of commit-sized units of work (a
  Plan Reviewer can review the plan itself before execution starts; route its feedback back to
  the Planner and send a summary of plan feedback to the user).
- **Worker**: a resident agent (kept alive across the reviewer round for a given unit) that
  implements one unit of work.
- **Reviewers (1..N)**: spawn multiple reviewer agents in parallel against the Worker's output —
  e.g. correctness, simplification/efficiency, and test coverage as separate reviewer passes.
  These can be ephemeral (fresh agent per round).
- **Synthesise**: reconcile the reviewers' findings into one set of required changes.
- **Pass? gate**: if synthesised feedback has no blocking issues, finalize and commit that unit
  with its own commit message, then move to the next planned unit. If it fails, send the
  synthesised feedback back to the Worker as another round on the same unit (don't restart from
  the Planner unless the feedback reveals the plan itself was wrong).

Net effect: one commit per feature/unit, each vetted by multiple reviewer passes before it lands,
rather than a single large uncommitted or unreviewed diff at the end.

## Verifying UI work: visual recreation (the main way to verify)

For any unit that changes UI, the primary verification is a **visual recreation**: render the real
components with mock data and look at a screenshot. Typecheck and unit tests are necessary but do not
count as verifying how it looks. Workers should do this before reporting, and I re-do it (or open the
image for the user) when the user asks to see it.

1. Add a **temporary** preview route (e.g. `apps/web/app/zz-preview/page.tsx`) that imports the real
   components and renders them with realistic mock props: populated, empty, capped/failed, long
   names/links. Put context around them (page background, a mock frame for panels/drawers that need a
   session or client state) but never reimplement the component itself.
2. Start the dev server in the background with dummy env vars the app needs to boot (e.g.
   `CONVEX_URL=https://dummy.convex.cloud CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY=x NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 bunx next dev -p <port>`),
   wait for "Ready", and `curl` the route for a 200.
3. Screenshot with headless Chrome, not the preview MCP tools (those time out):
   `"/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome" --headless=new --disable-gpu --hide-scrollbars --force-device-scale-factor=2 --virtual-time-budget=6000 --window-size=<w>,<h> --screenshot=/tmp/<name>.png <url>`
   Take a wide desktop shot and a narrow one. Headless Chrome enforces a minimum window width, so a
   narrow shot can come out horizontally clipped; for true 320px checks render inside a 320px-wide
   iframe or measure element widths, and say so rather than treating clipping as a bug.
4. **Read the PNG** (the Read tool shows images) and actually look at it: hierarchy, spacing, truncation,
   overflow, alignment, tap targets, copy. Report what was seen versus what was not verified
   (hover/focus states, real clipboard/share, animations, Safari-only behavior, the real page behind auth).
5. For the user, `open` the desktop screenshot (copy it to `~/Downloads/<name>.png` first) since they
   can't see tool-output images.
6. **Clean up before committing**: stop the dev server (`pkill -f "next dev -p <port>"`), delete the
   preview route, temp public files and stray `.next` artifacts, and confirm `git status` shows only
   intended changes. Never commit a preview route or mocks.

# Mandatory visual + local-server verification (every agent, every run)

Applies to any task that changes code a user can see or that the running app depends on. No unit of
work is "done" until both of these have happened and been reported:

1. **Run it against the local server.** Start the real dev server (and `npx convex dev` when Convex
   code changed) in this worktree, wait for "Ready", and exercise the changed path end to end: `curl`
   the route for the expected status and hit changed API routes. A passing typecheck/lint/build alone
   does not count.
2. **Verify visually with a screenshot.** Follow the visual-recreation steps above (headless Chrome,
   wide + narrow shot), then Read the PNG and look at it. For pages behind auth, use a temporary
   preview route with mock data. Non-UI changes still get a screenshot of the affected page to prove
   nothing regressed.
3. **Report** what was seen, what was not verified (hover/focus, auth-gated pages, animations), and
   the screenshot path. If the server can't boot (e.g. missing env vars), say so explicitly and fix
   the env first (see below); never claim success without having run it.
4. Clean up (stop the server, delete preview routes/temp files) before committing.

Env vars: each worktree needs its own copy of the gitignored `.env*` files. If `.env.local` is
missing in the current worktree, symlink it from the canonical copy at `~/.config/avian/.env.local`
(`ln -s ~/.config/avian/.env.local .env.local`) before starting the server.

+    return CheckVerdict("intent", v.preserved, f"judge ({v.model or 'unknown model'}; intent from {src}): {v.reason}",
+                        {"judge_model": v.model, "intent_source": c.intent_source})
+
+
+def held_out_cases(st: BisectState) -> list[str]:
+    if st.spec and st.spec.held_out:
+        return list(st.spec.held_out)
+    from .intake import load_cases
+    return [c.id for c in load_cases(st.repo) if c.held_out]
+
+
+def verify_fix(st: BisectState, runner: Runner, vin: VerifierInput, judge: IntentJudge | None = None) -> VerifyResult:
+    """Run the four checks on `vin.commit`. Resolves shas up front; never mutates `st` (see record_verification)."""
+    if not st.spec or not st.spec.cases:
+        raise ValueError("investigation has no eval cases")
+    fix = _git_out(vin.repo, "rev-parse", "--verify", f"{vin.commit}^{{commit}}").strip()
+    base = _git_out(vin.repo, "rev-parse", "--verify", f"{vin.base or st.bad_sha or 'HEAD'}^{{commit}}").strip()
+    run_id, before, saved = f"{st.id}-verify-{fix[:10]}", runner.eval_rounds, runner.signature
+    out = VerifyResult(fix, vin.branch)
+    try:
+        with step_span("verify_fix", fix=fix, base=base):
+            out.checks = [check_target(runner, st, fix, run_id), check_regression(runner, st, fix, base, run_id),
+                          check_held_out(runner, fix, held_out_cases(st), run_id), check_intent(st, vin, base, judge)]
+    finally:
+        runner.signature = saved
+    out.eval_rounds = runner.eval_rounds - before
+    return out
+
+
+def record_verification(store: StateStore, st: BisectState, vin: VerifierInput, res: VerifyResult) -> FixAttempt:
+    """Store the result on the matching FixAttempt (by branch, else a new one) and in metrics; moves the investigation
+    to `verifying` when the state machine allows it."""
+    reg, held, intent = res.check("regression"), res.check("held_out"), res.check("intent")
+    att = next((a for a in st.fix_attempts if vin.branch and a.branch == vin.branch), None)
+    if att is None:
+        att = FixAttempt(branch=vin.branch or res.commit, attempt=len(st.fix_attempts) + 1)
+        st.fix_attempts.append(att)
+    att.eval_score = reg.data.get("score") if reg else None
+    att.held_out_score = held.data.get("pass_rate") if held else None
+    att.intent_test_passed = intent.passed if intent else None
+    st.metrics.setdefault("verify_fix", {})[res.commit] = res.to_dict()
+    st.metrics["eval_rounds"] = st.metrics.get("eval_rounds", 0) + res.eval_rounds
+    st.metrics["cost_usd"] = round(st.metrics["eval_rounds"] * COST_PER_RUN_USD, 4)
+    if st.status in ("culprit_found", "fixing"):
+        store.set_status(st, "verifying")
+    else:
+        store.save(st)
+    return att
+
+
+def describe_verification(res: VerifyResult) -> list[str]:
+    mark = {True: "PASS", False: "FAIL", None: "INCONCLUSIVE"}
+    head = {True: "VERIFIED", False: "NOT VERIFIED", None: "INCONCLUSIVE"}[res.passed]
+    lines = [f"fix {res.commit[:10]}" + (f" ({res.branch})" if res.branch else "") + f": {head}"
+             f"  eval rounds={res.eval_rounds}"]
+    lines += [f"  [{mark[c.passed]}] {c.name}: {c.detail}" for c in res.checks]
+    return lines

## boardui
BoardUI is a React + Tailwind CSS v4 design system (Next.js first) with free components and paid Pro components/templates. This server installs component source directly into the user's project — no terminal needed.

Typical flow:
1. In a project without BoardUI, call init_boardui once (installs Tailwind v4 + runtime deps, writes styles/ and utils/).
2. Discover with list_components; read source/props with get_component; get working code with get_usage_examples.
3. Install with install_components — it writes the files and installs npm deps.

Component names are exact — when unsure, call list_components instead of guessing.

## RTL Support

BoardUI supports Arabic, Hebrew, and other right-to-left languages across free components, Pro blocks, and templates. The same source handles RTL and LTR; there is no RTL CLI flag or separate component version.

1. Read get_component and get_usage_examples for the free `direction` item. Install it with install_components (stdio), or write its source and dependencies yourself (read-only HTTP). CLI equivalent: `npx boardui@latest add direction`.
2. Wrap the app with DirectionProvider using an explicit BCP 47 locale: `ar` for Arabic, `he` for Hebrew, `en-US` for English. Set matching `lang` and `dir` on `<html>` for a full-app RTL layout. CSS dir alone does not configure React Aria keyboard navigation, calendars, or portalled menus.

```tsx
import { DirectionProvider } from "@/components/foundations/direction/direction";

export default function RootLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <html lang="ar" dir="rtl">
      <body>
        <DirectionProvider locale="ar">{children}</DirectionProvider>
      </body>
    </html>
  );
}
```

3. Use logical styles such as ps/pe, ms/me, start/end, and text-start/text-end. Mirror navigation arrows and drawer motion; preserve physical coordinates for charts, canvas, and decorative art. Custom portals should carry `dir={useDirection()}` on their root. Nest DirectionProvider for mixed-language regions.
4. Keep email addresses, URLs, OTP digits, and code LTR; isolate mixed text with bdi or dir=auto. Choose fonts with Arabic or Hebrew coverage and avoid extra letter spacing for Arabic. Translate application labels and accessible names in the application's translation layer; use Intl for dates, numbers, and currencies. Optional `template-copy` supplies TemplateCopyProvider for translating template display copy. Chinese (`zh-CN`) remains LTR.
